custom_capital_gains_tax.description:
Capital gains tax rate as a decimal between 0 and 1. Meaningful
when `tax_profile` is `custom_taxable` or `uk_taxable`; under
`uk_taxable` it is overridden to 0 for Gilts and QCBs. The
`us_taxable` profile does not apply a capital-gains adjustment —
post-tax yield under `us_taxable` is computed multiplicatively from
the effective income tax rate alone, deferring real capgain
handling until a dedicated US capital-gains field is added.

custom_income_tax.description:
Marginal income tax rate as a decimal between 0 and 1. Meaningful
when `tax_profile` is `custom_taxable` or `uk_taxable`; ignored
under `us_taxable`, which uses `federal_tax_rate` + `state_tax_rate`
+ `residing_state` per-bond rules instead.

federal_tax_rate.description:
Investor's marginal federal income tax rate, as a decimal 0-1.
Used only under the `us_taxable` profile (alongside
`state_tax_rate` + `residing_state`); ignored under
`custom_taxable`/`uk_taxable`, which use `custom_income_tax`.
Default 0.37.

filters.description:
The filters to apply, as a JSON object whose keys are fields to filter on or
operators. Send the object itself: this field is a nested object in the request
body, not a JSON-encoded string (`objective_function` is the only field on this
body that takes a JSON-encoded string).
Example: {"cusip": {"in": ["035240AQ3"]}, "maturity_date": {"less_than": "2030-01-01"}}

objective_function.description:
JSON-encoded objective function that defines the scoring formula for ranking bonds.
Contains a list of weighted terms, each referencing a field or an arithmetic expression.
Unlike `filters`, this field is a string: serialize the objective to JSON and send
the resulting string.
Example: {"terms": [{"term": {"type": "field", "field": "duration", "factor": 0.01}, "factor": 1.0}]}

`order_price`, `order_ytw` and `order_ytm` score the top of the book on the
scoring side (`objective_side`, or `side` when absent), falling back to price
estimates; an objective referencing them requires a scoring side (400 otherwise)
and risk group headers. `spread_to_benchmark` is an accepted optimizer alias for
`mid_ytw_spread_bps`, valid only inside the objective.

objective_side.description:
Which side of the book `objective_function`'s order fields score: 'sell' the
asks, 'buy' the bids ('both' is not accepted). Scoring-only — unlike `side` it
never filters the results, and it takes precedence over `side` for scoring.
Scoring order fields reads the live order book, so risk group headers are
still required.

page.description: The page number of the results to return. If not provided, the default is page 1.

page_size.description: The number of results to return per page. If not provided, the default is 100.

residing_state.description:
Two-letter state code of the investor's state of residence.
Example: "CA", "NY", "TX". Used only under the `us_taxable`
profile (drives per-bond state-tax exemptions); ignored under
`custom_taxable`/`uk_taxable`.

returns.description: The fields to return in the response.

risk_group_id.description:
The risk group ID to filter for tradable inventory. If left null,
and a single risk group exists for the organization, it will be
used as the default risk group. If left null, and more than one
risk group exists, the request will fail.

side.description:
Specify a side for inventory filters. Possible values:

- 'buy' will limit the results to bonds that have quotes to buy
  the instrument.
- 'sell' will limit the results to bonds that have quotes to sell
  the instrument.
- 'both' will limit the results to bonds that have quotes on both
  sides of the market, i.e. at least one quote to buy and one to sell.

Important note: If you are building a UI that leverages this API, you should be
especially cognizant that this value represents inventory side, not trade side.

A client who wants to purchase a bond will look for asks/offers where the
counterparty wants to sell. Hence, they should pass 'sell' to the API.

A client who wants to sell a bond will look for bids where the counterparty
wants to buy. Hence, they should pass 'buy' to the API.

When `objective_function` references `order_*` fields and `objective_side` is
absent, `side` also selects which side of the book those fields score ('both'
or no side is rejected with a 400). Use `objective_side` to choose the scoring
side independently of this filter.

sort_by.description:
The fields to sort the results by. Each field can optionally specify a direction
by appending '.asc' or '.desc'. If no direction is specified, defaults to ascending order.

state_tax_rate.description:
Investor's marginal state income tax rate, as a decimal 0-1.
Used only under the `us_taxable` profile; ignored under
`custom_taxable`/`uk_taxable`.

tax_profile.description:
Tax profile classification controlling how post-tax yield fields
and the post-tax objective term are computed.

- `us_taxable` (default): post-tax yield is the pre-tax yield
  multiplied by `(1 - effective_tax_rate)`, where
  `effective_tax_rate` is the per-bond combination of
  `federal_tax_rate` + `state_tax_rate` + `residing_state` with
  treasury, US-territory, state-exempt-agency, and muni
  federal/state exemption carve-outs applied per bond. Capital
  gains is not applied under this profile (deferred until a real
  US capgain field is defined).
- `custom_taxable`: post-tax yield is the bivariate Taylor
  expansion of after-tax YTW evaluated at constants
  (`s = custom_income_tax`, `g = custom_capital_gains_tax`).
  Federal/state/residing-state are ignored.
- `uk_taxable`: same Taylor expansion as `custom_taxable`
  (using `custom_income_tax` and `custom_capital_gains_tax`), but
  the capital-gains rate is forced to 0 for instruments exempt from
  UK capital gains tax — Gilts (`ice_sector_1 = Sovereign` and
  `currency = GBP`) and QCBs (`qcb_indicator = true`). Income tax
  still applies to exempt instruments.
- `non_taxable`: no tax is applied to any instrument. Post-tax yield
  equals the pre-tax yield and tax-equivalent yield receives no
  gross-up. All rate fields are ignored.

trade_size.description:
Filtering by trade_size will only return `asks` and `bids` that
would completely fill an order of the specified quantity. More
specifically, it will return quotes where the minimum quantity is
less than or equal to the specified trade_size and the total
quantity is greater than or equal to the specified trade_size.
Optionally, set value to "lowest" to get all the quotes sorted from
least to greatest `min_quantity`.

use_close_data_after_hours.description:
Whether to use close data after market hours. When false (default),
only reference data is returned when market is closed. When true,
orders are shown as available even after market close (9:30 AM - 4:00 PM EST/EDT, Monday-Friday).

InventoryFilter.description:
In a filter object, each key is either a field to filter on or an operator.
Each value is either a filter condition object or, in the case of certain
operators, an array of filter objects.

Some of the fields which can be filtered on are explicitly defined on this schema.
Any of the other fields in the reference data model can be used as an
InventoryFilter key.

and.description: Filter operator key with array value of filter objects to be combined with AND.

not.description: Filter operator key with a filter object to be negated.

objective_score.description:
Filter on the computed objective score. Requires an
`objective_function` in the request — the score is computed from
it per bond. Supports only the numeric comparison operators
(equal_to, not_equal_to, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal_to,
less_than, less_than_or_equal_to) and is_null, with numeric
values. Combine with `sort_by: ["objective_score.desc"]` to rank
and threshold in one query.

or.description: Filter operator key with array value of filter objects to be combined with OR.

ends_with.description: String to end with in the filter.

greater_than.description: Greater than value for the filter.

greater_than_or_equal_to.description: Greater than or equal to value for the filter.

in.description: Array of values for the filter.

in_filter_list.description: Filter by values from a named filter list. The value is the filter list ID (e.g., "list_01ABC123").

includes.description: String to include in the filter.

is_null.description: Boolean to filter for null / not-null values.

less_than.description: Less than value for the filter.

less_than_or_equal_to.description: Less than or equal to value for the filter.

not_equal_to.description: Not equal to value for the filter.

not_in.description: Array of values not to include in the filter.

not_in_filter_list.description: Exclude values that are in a named filter list. The value is the filter list ID (e.g., "list_01ABC123").

not_includes.description: String not to include in the filter.

starts_with.description: String to start with in the filter.

InventoryReturnField.description:
A field that can be requested in the `returns` array. Fields come from
three distinct sources — choose based on whether you want the live
market or an evaluated model price:

1. LIVE ORDER BOOK (real, executable quotes from dealers):
   - `bids` / `asks`: full depth — every individual quote with its own
     price, quantity, min_quantity, and yield_to_worst.
   - `best_ask_ytw`: the live top-of-book ask yield — the YTW of the
     best offer (lowest price, i.e. highest yield). Use this (or read
     `asks`) for "what's the yield on this bond / the best offer to buy
     at".
   - `best_bid_ytw`: the live top-of-book bid yield — the YTW of the
     best bid (highest price, i.e. lowest yield). Use this (or read
     `bids`) for "what could I sell this at".
   - `best_ask_price` / `best_bid_price`: the live top-of-book ask/bid
     PRICE — the price of the same best offer/bid as `best_ask_ytw` /
     `best_bid_ytw`. Use these (or read `asks` / `bids`) for "what's the
     price of the best offer / what could I sell this at"; do NOT use the
     deprecated `ask_price` / `bid_price`, which are evaluated-model
     values, not live quotes.
   - `best_ask_post_tax_ytw` / `best_bid_post_tax_ytw`,
     `best_ask_tax_equivalent_yield` / `best_bid_tax_equivalent_yield`,
     `market_spread_*`: derived from the live order book.

2. EVALUATED MODEL (price-estimates feed — a modeled valuation, NOT a
   live tradable quote):
   - `eval_price` / `eval_ytw` / `eval_ytm`: the mid evaluated value.
   - `eval_bid_*` / `eval_ask_*` / `eval_mid_*` (price, ytw, ytm, ytc,
     spreads, oas): the evaluated curve's bid/ask/mid values. These are
     model outputs, not order-book quotes.
   - `ask_eval_ytw_diff` / `bid_eval_ytw_diff` (and the `_price_diff`
     variants): live best book yield/price MINUS the evaluated value.

3. REFERENCE / STATIC DATA: identifiers, descriptive, ratings, dates,
   call schedule, etc. (`isin`, `cusip`, `issuer`, `coupon`, ...).

DEPRECATED — a non-deprecated alternative always exists, so always find
it and use it instead: the bare `bid_*` / `ask_*` / `mid_*` families
(`ask_ytw`, `bid_ytw`, `mid_ytw`, `ask_price`, `bid_price`, `ask_oas`,
`ask_ytw_spread_bps`, ...) are EVALUATED-MODEL values, NOT live
order-book quotes despite the bid/ask naming. Each is an exact alias of
its `eval_`-prefixed counterpart (e.g. `ask_ytw` == `eval_ask_ytw`,
`ask_price` == `eval_ask_price`). They are retained only for backward
compatibility and will be removed. For the evaluated value use the
explicit `eval_*` name (`eval_ask_price`, `eval_ask_ytw`, ...); for the
live top-of-book use `best_ask_price` / `best_bid_price` /
`best_ask_ytw` / `best_bid_ytw` or the `asks` / `bids` arrays.
